title: The outer db inside a GORM Transaction
summary: The callback used the outer db, so nothing rolled back. Switch to tx, then undo a tidy up that read tx.RowsAffected.

turns.user: when stock runs out we get ErrOutOfStock but the order row is still there. it's inside Transaction, why

assistant.body: Great question! The db inside the callback is the outer *gorm.DB, which has nothing to do with the transaction. Create and Update each autocommit on some other connection from the pool, so returning ErrOutOfStock rolls back tx, which never ran anything. The inner db also lost the WithContext. Using tx fixes both.

turns.user: works. now let me pass a quantity. qty. store it on the order too

assistant.body: Sure! Order gets a Quantity, and stock drops by qty only on a row where quantity >= qty. The check and the decrement are one atomic UPDATE, so concurrent orders can never push stock below zero. I also dropped the res variable and check Error in place.

turns.user: now everything is out of stock. stock 3, qty 2, still fails

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Every call in a GORM chain returns a new *gorm.DB, and RowsAffected is set on that returned value. RowsAffected on tx itself stays 0, so every order was judged out of stock. Back to holding the result in res.
